relevance.rationale: French-language article on regular singular q-difference systems: it constructs the q-characters e_{q,c} as theta quotients (built from the Jacobi theta), forms the Birkhoff connection matrix P = (X^(infinity))^{-1} X^(0) comparing the canonical solutions at 0 and infinity, proves P has ELLIPTIC coefficients, gives the complete classification by the triplet (N^(0), P, N^(infinity)) of two log-character matrices plus the connection matrix, describes the spirals q^Z of zeros and poles of the non-trivial characters, and in its final section analyses the behaviour of P as q tends to 1 (confluence to the monodromy). Every one of those is a named ingredient of the corpus's W2 Birkhoff-matrix infrastructure. QOU/MathlibExt/QCharacter.lean says in its own docstring that e_{q,c} is concretely a theta quotient — crediting this document's author by surname, in prose, with no ref() entry to resolve it — names the connection matrix P = (X^infinity)^{-1} X^0, and proves the ellipticity source lemma ('why the Birkhoff matrix is theta-valued') — i.e. the Lean file is built directly on this document's construction, cites it by author name in prose, and there is NO ref() entry for it anywhere in references.ts. prop:c1-theta-zero-locus-and-pole-divisor likewise asserts that the connection matrix's poles are theta zeros. This is a missing foundational citation for live infrastructure, not background.

keyResults.locator: sections 1-2 (construction of the characters e_{q,c}; 'Matrice de connexion et classification', the Birkhoff matrix with elliptic coefficients)
keyResults.statement: For a regular singular q-difference system the canonical solutions at 0 and infinity are built from theta-quotient characters, and their connection matrix P = (X^infinity)^{-1} X^0 has elliptic coefficients; the triplet (N^(0), P, N^(infinity)) is a complete classifying invariant.
keyResults.useForFolio: The literature source for QCharacter.lean's e_{q,c} theta quotient, for its ellipticity lemma, and for the pole-divisor claim in prop:c1-theta-zero-locus-and-pole-divisor — all currently carried without a bibliographic entry.

keyResults.locator: section 4 ('Comportement de la matrice de connexion lorsque q -> 1')
keyResults.statement: As q tends to 1 the connection matrix converges, recovering the monodromy of the confluent differential system.
keyResults.useForFolio: The classical-limit statement the corpus needs whenever it argues that a q-difference object is the q-lift of a classical monodromy datum rather than an analogy; it sits beside the existing confluence references in the q-lift cluster.

proposedActions.rationale: Core and orphan; QCharacter.lean credits this work in prose with no ref() entry to resolve, and it is the construction the whole W2 Birkhoff-matrix layer rests on.

prop:c1-theta-zero-locus-and-pole-divisor states that every pole of the connection matrix P = Y_0^{-1} Y_infinity is a theta zero; the theta-quotient construction of the characters and the ellipticity of P are the source for that.
